findings.reason: The protected solution is clear, conventional, and interview-ready. Its parent and size maps, add and find helpers, representative names, union-by-size swap, and aligned-word loop expose the disjoint-set state and transitive decision directly without graph-search repetition or unnecessary classes.

Each declared pair creates an undirected connectivity edge, and every union merges exactly the two components containing its endpoints. Consequently, all words connected by a pair chain obtain one representative, while different components remain separate. Union by size changes only the representative choice, and path compression preserves membership. Identical aligned words pass reflexively even when absent from the structure; distinct words pass only when both are present and have the same representative, exactly implementing symmetric and transitive similarity.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 737, Python, and the native areSentencesSimilarTwo(sentence1, sentence2, similarPairs) interface. Authenticated source evidence confirms one-to-1000-word sentence arrays, one-to-20-character English-letter words, zero-to-2000 two-word similarity pairs with one-to-20-character English-letter endpoints, equal-length necessity, aligned comparison, reflexive equality, undirected pair connectivity, transitive chains, and the Boolean sentence result.

The protected app source and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2065830532 are algorithmically identical: both use the same lazy word insertion, iterative root search, full path compression, union by component size, equal-word bypass, presence checks, and representative comparison. Their only structural differences are the required Solution.areSentencesSimilarTwo wrapper and Python typing dialect.

The unchanged three authored workloads grow n + p from 8 to 72, building one long similarity chain and repeatedly asking whether its endpoints are connected. In a fresh real-test run, the exact protected source passed all thirteen visible correctness cases and all three performance tiers with relative growth exponent -0.01 and a 0.94x largest runtime ratio. A correct control that launches a fresh graph traversal for every aligned endpoint pair matched every output but failed only performance with relative growth exponent +0.90, distinguishing near-linear union-find preprocessing from quadratic repeated connectivity search.

The Approach accurately maps transitive similarity to graph components, derives union by size and path compression, handles equal and absent words, and proves component equality is necessary and sufficient. Its O((n+p) alpha(w)) time and O(w) auxiliary-space claims match the protected implementation and branch manifest; the inverse-Ackermann symbol is now rendered with proper LaTeX notation.

The modular Reference preserves the source's sentence-to-array illustration, declared similarity-pair model, Boolean objective, two positional conditions, reflexive rule, and transitive-chain example. It includes all three exact source examples with every explanation step, all seven constraints, and the source-native connected-component hint.

Authenticated Premium source review verified exactly three explained examples, two definition bullets, seven constraints, no images or tables, and one provider hint. source_fidelity.json binds the live statement hash e168eb2e9b24ad4cf891ff4c1d42b80f05e6d699a7892ee53c5bbe30c1fc59ce and every composed Reference section; the independent validator reports verified with no errors.
